text: A pulse of 140 beats/min is a {{c1::normal::normal or life-threatening}} finding in an infant, but the same rate in a 30-year-old adult signals a {{c1::life-threatening::normal or life-threatening}} condition.
verified_by: p683 prose, verbatim: "Finding a pulse rate of 140 beats/min ... is usually normal for an infant. However, for a 30-year-old adult, the same values would likely signal the presence of a life-threatening condition." Corroborated on the rendered plate figures/TABLE_7_1.png: infant pulse 100 to 160 (140 inside), adult pulse 60 to 100 (140 far outside), neonate pulse floor 100. The prose's companion figure of 60 breaths/min was REMOVED by the editor: TABLE 7-1 caps infant respirations at 50 and puts 60 only in the neonate band, so the book contradicts itself on that digit.

text:
A neonate's body weight follows a predictable course:

At birth: {{c1::6 to 8 lb (3 to 3.5 kg)}}

First week: falls {{c1::5% to 10%}} from fluid loss

Second week onward: gains about {{c1::1 ounce (30 g) per day}}

Doubles birth weight by {{c1::4 to 6 months}}

Triples birth weight by {{c1::1 year}}

visual_source.note: figure extracted from the source PDF and attached to this card (scripts/attach_figures.py --to-cards).

stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: A neonate's head accounts for about {{c1::25%}} of total body weight, which is why neonates and infants tend to land {{c2::headfirst}} when they fall.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Neonates are primarily {{c1::nose::nose or mouth}} breathers, and infants younger than {{c2::6 months::age}} are especially susceptible to congestion that can lead to viral upper respiratory infections.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: You are dispatched for a 2-month-old who is reportedly choking. The mouth and throat are clear, yet the infant is still struggling to breathe, so you check next for obstruction of {{c1::the nasal passages::anatomic site}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text:
Airway obstruction is more common in infants than in older children and adults. Compared with an adult, what is anatomically different about an infant's airway and head?

{{c1::a larger tongue relative to the size of the oral cavity}}

{{c1::a proportionally shorter and narrower airway}}

{{c1::a proportionally oversized occiput}}

{{c1::a more flexible trachea}}
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: In an infant, the EMT preserves airway patency through proper positioning, because both {{c1::hyperextending}} and {{c1::hyperflexing}} the head and neck can easily produce an airway obstruction.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: An infant's rib cage is {{c1::less::more or less}} rigid and the ribs sit {{c1::horizontally::orientation}}, which explains the {{c2::diaphragmatic (belly) breathing}} typically seen in infants.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: {{c1::Barotrauma}} is {{c2::pressure-induced trauma to the lungs}}, and in an infant the cause is {{c3::forceful ventilations and overinflation}} with a bag-mask.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text:
In a healthy, full-term newborn, four reflexes are present at birth:

{{c1::Moro (startle)}}

{{c1::palmar grasp}}

{{c1::rooting}}

{{c1::sucking}}
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text:
Name the newborn reflex from how it presents:

The arms fly open wide and the fingers spread, as if grabbing at something = the {{c1::Moro}} reflex

Something touches the cheek and the head turns toward the touch = the {{c1::rooting}} reflex
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: {{c1::Fontanelles::structures}} are the {{c2::flexible fibrous gaps between cranial bones}}, and they let the newborn's head {{c3::change shape}} as it passes through the narrow birth canal.

text:
The fontanelles do not close at the same age:

Posterior fontanelle → closes by {{c1::the third month}}

Anterior fontanelle → closes between {{c1::9 and 18 months}}

text: In an infant with an open fontanelle, a {{c1::depressed::depressed or bulging}} fontanelle may indicate {{c2::dehydration}}, whereas a {{c1::bulging::depressed or bulging}} fontanelle often signals {{c2::increased intracranial pressure}}.

text: Teething (baby teeth breaking through the gums) can be {{c1::painful}} and is sometimes accompanied by a {{c1::low-grade}} fever.

text:
Match each characteristic to the age at which it typically appears in an infant:

Reaches arms out to people; drools → {{c1::4 months}}

Sleeps throughout the night; distinguishes family members from strangers → {{c1::5 months}}

Recognizes familiar faces; uses the eyes to track objects and people → {{c1::2 months}}

Begins teething; sits upright; speaks one-syllable words → {{c1::6 months}}

Brings objects to the mouth; smiles and frowns → {{c1::3 months}}
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text:
Match each infant characteristic to the age at which it typically appears:

Pulls self up to stand; explores objects by placing them in the mouth → {{c1::9 months}}

Knows his or her name; walks → {{c1::12 months}}

Afraid of strangers; displays mood swings → {{c1::7 months}}

Begins to walk without assistance; becomes frustrated by restrictions → {{c1::11 months}}

Responds to "no"; can sit alone; plays peek-a-boo → {{c1::8 months}}

Responds to his or her name; crawls efficiently → {{c1::10 months}}

text: In older infants, {{c1::separation anxiety}} is common, marked by {{c2::clingy behavior}} and {{c2::fear of unfamiliar places and people}}, and typically peaking between {{c3::10 and 18 months}} of age.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: The psychosocial stage of {{c1::trust versus mistrust}} begins at {{c2::birth}} and concludes at approximately {{c2::18 months}} of age.

text: A toddler's and preschooler's lungs keep adding terminal bronchioles and alveoli, but the {{c1::musculature}} of those lungs is still poorly developed, so they cannot sustain {{c2::deep or rapid respirations::breathing pattern}} for long.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: In toddlers the loss of {{c1::passive immunity}} plus constant exposure to other children brings frequent viral colds, which often show up as {{c2::upper respiratory symptoms}} or {{c2::gastrointestinal distress}}. The antibodies those repeated infections generate become {{c3::acquired immunity}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: By the end of the preschooler stage, a child's brain weighs roughly {{c1::90%::percentage}} of its adult weight.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Toddlers have the neuromuscular ability to control the bladder by {{c1::12 to 15 months::age range}}, but many are not psychologically ready for toilet training until {{c2::18 to 30 months::age range}}. On average, toilet training is complete at {{c3::28 months::age}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Most children have mastered basic language skills by the age of {{c1::36 months::age}}, and understand full sentences by {{c2::3 or 4 years::age}}.

visual_source.note: figure extracted from the source PDF and attached to this card (scripts/attach_figures.py --to-cards).

stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Toddlers begin to understand the concept of cause and effect at about {{c1::18 to 24 months::age range}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: You are treating a severely injured child when the father, overwhelmed by fear, begins to panic and can no longer answer your questions. On this call the father has become a {{c1::secondary patient::role on scene}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Each year a school-age child gains about {{c1::4 pounds (2 kg)::weight}} and grows about {{c2::2.5 inches (6 cm)::height}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text:
School-age children develop moral reasoning in three levels, each answering to a different influence:

{{c1::Preconventional}} → {{c2::external forces such as parental discipline}}

{{c1::Conventional}} → {{c2::the approval of peers and society}}

{{c1::Postconventional}} → {{c2::an internalized moral compass (conscience)}}
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: {{c1::Self-concept}} is {{c2::our perception of ourselves}}, whereas {{c1::self-esteem}} is {{c2::how we feel about ourselves}} and how we fit in with our peers.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text:
The adolescent growth spurt lasts {{c2::2 to 3 years::duration}} and proceeds in a fixed order:

{{c1::hands and feet}} → {{c1::long bones of the extremities}} → {{c1::torso}}

visual_source.note: figure extracted from the source PDF and attached to this card (scripts/attach_figures.py --to-cards).

stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Girls finish the adolescent growth spurt by about {{c1::16 years}}, whereas boys typically reach their growth peak by {{c1::18 years}} and generally become {{c1::taller::taller or shorter}} than girls.

visual_source.note: figure extracted from the source PDF and attached to this card (scripts/attach_figures.py --to-cards).

stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: The adolescent milestone called {{c1::menarche}} is {{c2::the first menstrual bleeding}}, and reaching it before the adolescent years is {{c3::not uncommon::uncommon or not uncommon}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text:
The leading cause of death changes with age:

All age groups younger than 44 years → {{c1::unintentional injury}}

Ages 45 to 64 years → {{c2::cancer}}, not heart disease
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Cardiac function declines with age largely because of {{c1::atherosclerosis::vascular condition}}, a buildup of {{c2::cholesterol and calcium::two substances}} along the inner walls of blood vessels that forms plaque.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: More than {{c1::60%::percentage}} of people older than {{c1::65 years::age}} have atherosclerotic disease.

visual_source.note: figure extracted from the source PDF and attached to this card (scripts/attach_figures.py --to-cards).

stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text:
Beyond atherosclerosis, aging weakens the older adult's heart in three ways:

{{c1::the heart rate decreases}}

{{c1::cardiac output declines}}

{{c1::the ability to increase cardiac output on demand diminishes}}
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Because the older adult's vascular system stiffens, blood vessels cannot dilate and contract effectively, so {{c1::diastolic::systolic or diastolic}} blood pressure {{c1::increases::increases or decreases}} and the heart must work harder against vascular resistance.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Human blood cells originate in the bone marrow, but with advancing age that marrow is replaced by {{c1::fatty tissue}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text:
Classify each of the four ways aging changes the older adult's respiratory system:

Size of the airway: {{c1::increases::increases or decreases}}

Surface area of the alveoli: {{c1::decreases::increases or decreases}}

Elasticity of the lungs: {{c1::decreases::increases or decreases}}

Strength of the intercostal muscles and diaphragm: {{c1::decreases::increases or decreases}}
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: {{c1::Vital capacity}} is the volume of air moved during {{c2::the deepest inspiration and expiration}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: By age {{c1::75::age}}, an older adult's vital capacity has declined to about {{c1::50%::percentage}} of that of a young adult.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text:
With age, five protective features of the upper airway weaken:

{{c1::the cough reflex}}

{{c1::the gag reflex}}

{{c1::the ability to clear secretions}}

{{c1::the cilia that line the airway}}

{{c1::sensation within the airway}}
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: As the structures protecting the upper airway lose function with age, the older adult is at greater risk of {{c1::aspiration}} and {{c1::airway obstruction}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: With age, taste buds become less sensitive to {{c1::salty}} and {{c1::sweet}} foods, and food may be perceived as bland and flavorless because the sense of {{c2::smell}} fades along with taste.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: {{c1::Peristalsis}} is the process in which intestinal contractions {{c2::move food along the digestive tract}}, and with age it {{c3::slows::speeds up or slows}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Age-related change in peristalsis leaves an older adult prone to {{c1::constipation::bowel}} and/or {{c1::suppressed feelings of hunger::appetite}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: In older adults, blood flow to the intestines can drop by as much as {{c1::50%}}, so the extraction of {{c2::vitamins}} and {{c2::minerals}} from digested food wanes.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Between the ages of 20 and 90 years, the kidneys decrease in size by {{c1::20%}} and their filtration capabilities decline by as much as {{c1::50%}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: Aging reduces renal function in two ways: the kidneys become less able to {{c1::remove waste}} from the body and less able to {{c1::conserve fluids}} when needed.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: By the time a person is {{c1::80}} years of age, the brain has decreased in weight by as much as {{c2::10% to 20%}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: In an older adult, the brain's metabolic rate and oxygen consumption remain {{c1::unchanged::increased, decreased, or unchanged}}.
stage: draft(unit agent) -> independent unit editor -> global consolidation -> verify_report -> check_cards gate -> 2 independent batch judges

text: In an older adult, age-related {{c1::shrinkage}} of the brain opens a void between the brain and the outermost layer of the meninges, so a rapid or forceful shift of the brain can tear the {{c2::bridging veins}}.
